bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42485333 (glib): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 5 found by fuzz target fuzz_uri_parse [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42485333
bug_description.normalized: GLib's vulnerable IPv6-literal host parser handles RFC 6874 zone identifiers with ad hoc '%' logic instead of splitting, validating, and decoding the ZoneID. Under non-strict parsing, `uri_cleanup()` rewrites the embedded space inside the bracketed host to `%20`; `parse_host()` then validates only the truncated prefix before `%`, accepts `":"` as an IPv6 literal, and preserves the malformed suffix in `uri->host`. When `g_uri_to_string()` later reserializes that host, `_uri_encoder()` reaches the trailing `0xF8`, treats the one-byte tail as a positive UTF-8 result, uses `g_utf8_skip[0xF8] == 5`, and drives the observed 5-byte read from the `parse_host()` heap buffer.

source.description: First project-side input consumption on the crashing path that creates vulnerability-relevant state: `uri_cleanup()` rewrites the attacker's literal space inside the bracketed host into `%20`, introducing the `%` later treated as a zone-ID delimiter.
source.value_from: Stage 01 reproduced the crash on the exact 9-byte witness in `poc` (`59 3a 2f 2f 5b 3a 20 f8 5d`, SHA-256 `cabafa65f041d3904e8c4da4a1cd11129bad6377be5a51ef3b652f2f0228663c`). Because the call uses `G_URI_FLAGS_NONE` and the witness contains a literal space, `g_uri_split_internal()` takes the non-strict cleanup path and rewrites the URI bytes to `59 3a 2f 2f 5b 3a 25 32 30 f8 5d` before host parsing.

root_cause.description: The vulnerable scope-ID handling treats the first `%` as a temporary terminator and validates only the truncated prefix. The later block at lines 416-423 then restores the suffix with only secondary `%` and `%25` checks instead of parsing and decoding a ZoneID.
root_cause.note: The fix patch replaces this ad hoc handling with `parse_ip_literal()` plus `uri_decode()` on a separately split zone substring. That patch alignment is static only: Stage 01 reproduced the vulnerable build but did not execute the fixed build.

sink.description: ASan crash site. During URI reserialization, `g_string_insert_len()` performs the witnessed 5-byte read from data derived from the `parse_host()` heap buffer.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `READ of size 5` at this line and shows the call chain `g_string_append_uri_escaped() -> _uri_encoder() -> g_string_append_len() -> g_string_insert_len()`. Step 13 fixes that copy length at 5 from `g_utf8_skip[0xF8]`, so this `memcpy` reads 5 bytes starting at the trailing `0xF8` in the 6-byte region allocated in `parse_host()` at `glib/guri.c:405`; ASan reports the first invalid byte immediately to the right of that region.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant heap state is the `addr` buffer holding the 5 inner bytes of the cleaned bracketed host (`:%20<0xF8>` plus NUL). The later overread consumes bytes from this same allocation after parser acceptance and propagation.

cleanup_applied.description: The crashing call uses `G_URI_FLAGS_NONE` and the witness contains a literal space, so this branch forces `uri_cleanup()` before authority parsing.

parser_admitted.code: if (!parse_host (p, hostend - p, flags, host, error))
parser_admitted.description: After cleanup, the authority parser hands the cleaned bracketed host `[:%20<0xF8>]` to `parse_host()`. The saved vulnerable run proves this call returned success and later produced the host string reserialized by `g_uri_to_string()`.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness NUL-terminates the exact 9-byte witness and calls non-strict `g_uri_parse()`.
Because the URI contains a literal space, `uri_cleanup()` rewrites the bracketed host from `[: <0xF8>]` to `[:%20<0xF8>]`, and authority parsing passes that cleaned literal into `parse_host()`.

The parser copies `:%20<0xF8>` into a 6-byte heap buffer, truncates validation at the first `%`, accepts the truncated `":"` as IPv6, restores the malformed suffix, and returns the same allocation as the parsed host.

URI reserialization treats the surviving host as an IP literal and passes it into `g_string_append_uri_escaped()`. `_uri_encoder()` eventually reaches the trailing `0xF8`, the unsigned validated-character predicate selects `g_utf8_skip[0xF8] == 5`, and `g_string_insert_len()` performs the observed 5-byte overread from the `parse_host()` allocation.

fine_trace.code:
nul_terminated_data = (unsigned char *) g_strndup ((const gchar *) data, size);
test_with_flags ((const gchar *) nul_terminated_data, G_URI_FLAGS_NONE);
fine_trace.note: Harness step. The exact saved witness is the 9-byte file `59 3a 2f 2f 5b 3a 20 f8 5d`, which the harness NUL-terminates and passes to the non-strict `g_uri_parse()` call.

Source. Because the non-strict parser sees a literal space, `uri_cleanup()` rewrites that byte to `%20`. This creates the first `%` later consumed as a scope-ID delimiter and changes the URI bytes to `59 3a 2f 2f 5b 3a 25 32 30 f8 5d`.
The parser switches from the original witness to the cleaned copy, so all later authority parsing sees bracketed host bytes `[:%20<0xF8>]` rather than the original `[: <0xF8>]`.

fine_trace.code:
hostend = colon ? colon : path_start;
if (!parse_host (p, hostend - p, flags, host, error))
fine_trace.note: Authority parsing is on a bracketed host (`*p == '['`), so `parse_host()` receives the 7-byte cleaned literal `[:%20<0xF8>]`. Removing the brackets will therefore yield the 5-byte inner host `:%20<0xF8>`.
ASan allocation context. `g_strndup()` copies the inner 5 bytes `:%20<0xF8>` into heap buffer `addr`, allocating 6 addressable bytes including the trailing NUL.

Root cause begins. The cleanup-added `%` at offset 1 is treated as a scope-ID separator, so `pct` points inside `:%20<0xF8>` and the in-place NUL write truncates `addr` to the prefix `":"` before validation.

The only IPv6 guard now examines `":"`. `g_hostname_is_ip_address(":")` returns true because `ghostutils.c:705-763` enters the IPv6 colon path, sets `skipped = TRUE` for the bare-colon case, and succeeds at EOF; `strchr (addr, ':')` is also non-null, so rejection is skipped.

After that truncated prefix has been accepted, the code restores `%` into the same buffer, finds no second `%` in `20<f8>`, and skips the only decode path because the suffix starts with `%20` rather than `%25`. The malformed host therefore stays `:%20<0xF8>`.
Instead of rejecting or rebuilding from a validated zone identifier, `parse_host()` aliases the same 6-byte allocation as the parsed host.
The success path returns that same pointer through the caller-supplied `host` out-parameter; in `g_uri_parse_relative()` this parameter is `&uri->host` at `guri.c:1163-1166`.

During `g_uri_to_string()`, the surviving host still contains `:`, so GLib takes the IP-literal branch, adds surrounding brackets, and sends the same host buffer to URI escaping with only `:` allowed verbatim.

The escaping wrapper passes `_uri_encoder()` the same host pointer, `allow_utf8 = TRUE`, and a source-level length computed by `strlen (host)`. For the reconstructed host `:%20<0xF8>`, `strlen()` yields 5, so the encoder loop ends just after the trailing `0xF8` byte.

After earlier loop iterations consume `:%20`, `p` reaches the final byte `0xF8` with `end - p == 1`. `g_utf8_get_char_validated ((gchar *)p, 1)` returns the partial-sequence sentinel `(gunichar)-2`; because `gunichar` is `guint32`, the `> 0` test still succeeds, `g_utf8_skip[0xF8]` contributes `5`, and `_uri_encoder()` requests a 5-byte append from that tail pointer.

Sink. Step 13's `g_string_append_len (..., len = 5)` call forwards the same tail pointer and length into `g_string_insert_len()`, so this `memcpy` attempts to read 5 bytes beginning at the trailing `0xF8` in the allocation from step 5. The saved ASan trace reports that 5-byte read and places the first invalid byte immediately past the 6-byte region.

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch in `glib/guri.c` clearly targets the same ad hoc scope-ID parsing block covered by fine-trace steps 6-8, but Stage 01 only verified the vulnerable build. `patch_resolves` therefore remains false because fixed-version runtime confirmation is unavailable in Stage 02.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow on the exact 9-byte file in `poc` (`59 3a 2f 2f 5b 3a 20 f8 5d`). On that run, `uri_cleanup()` rewrites the embedded space to `%20`, `parse_host()` allocates the 6-byte host buffer from the cleaned inner bytes `:%20<0xF8>`, and `_uri_encoder()` later computes `len = 5` for the trailing `0xF8`, causing the crash in `g_string_insert_len()`.

format.name: raw URI witness
format.contract: The only verified trigger semantics are the exact 9-byte witness saved in `poc` (SHA-256 `cabafa65f041d3904e8c4da4a1cd11129bad6377be5a51ef3b652f2f0228663c`). Stage 01 shows that exact file is normalized to bytes `59 3a 2f 2f 5b 3a 25 32 30 f8 5d`, yields a `parse_host()` allocation for `:%20<0xF8>` plus NUL, and reaches `_uri_encoder()` with `strlen (host) == 5`. At the final byte `0xF8`, `g_utf8_get_char_validated ((gchar *)p, 1) > 0` and `g_utf8_skip[0xF8] == 5`, so `g_string_insert_len()` performs the observed 5-byte read. This GT does not generalize beyond that exact witness.
